facts.statement: The genus Pinacosuchus was named by Gilmore in 1942.
Pinacosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Pinacosuchus is classified within the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
The type species of the genus is Pinacosuchus mantiensis, described by Gilmore in 1942.
Fossils of Pinacosuchus have been found in the Late Cretaceous North Horn Formation of Utah, United States.
facts.quote: Fossils attributed to the genus have been reported from the Late Cretaceous North Horn Formation of Utah (United States).

facts.statement: Pinacosuchus is a small crocodylomorph characterized by spiky dermal armor, though it is known from only limited fossil remains.
facts.quote: Pinacosuchus has been described as a small-bodied crocodylomorph with spiky dermal armor, but it is known only from limited remains.

facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered at the "Lizard Locality" in the Manti National Forest, Emery County, Utah.
facts.quote: This specimen was discovered at the "Lizard Locality" in the Manti National Forest, Emery County, Utah.

facts.statement: The sacrum of the holotype specimen USNM 16592 measured only 14.3 mm in length.
facts.quote: The sacrum (the vertebra supporting the hips) of USNM 16592 was only 14.3 mm long.

facts.statement: Gilmore determined the specimen was an adult based on the absence of sutures on the neural arches of the vertebrae.
facts.quote: Gilmore regarded the specimen as an adult because the vertebrae lacked sutures for their neural arches, a sign of maturity.

facts.statement: The armor of Pinacosuchus includes five types of scutes: simple rectangular, ridged rooflike, thickened rectangular with sharp spines, small pointed spines, and elongate pointed spines.
facts.quote: Gilmore divided the armor into five categories: simple rectangular scutes; ridged rooflike scutes; thickened rectangular scutes with asymmetrically-positioned sharp spines overhanging the borders; small pointed spines with thickened bases; and more elongate pointed spines with thickened bases.

facts.statement: Pinacosuchus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
